For a long time I was running Win7 at home and had the OS pretty locked down from a privacy perspective. Since it’s [win7] installation I disabled any privacy reduction related things like CIEP, indexing, sending error reports, etc. I have my drive the OS sits on encrypted, OpenVPN installed on my WiFi router along with a second VPN provider running a client app on my local machine. I have Firefox pretty locked down with a bunch of recommended changes to the about:config, while running noscript, user agent spoofer, https everywhere, and a couple others etc.

Fast forward to last night; I’ve been on Voat as a lurker for a couple months after I decided rEddit sold out. I’ve been following the privacy related discussions concerning windows and made all the recommended changes as they have been coming out on Voat and other news sources. It seems every week the news just gets worse about windows, so I decided last night to make the switch to Linux.

I had a spare SSD drive from an old laptop and decided to install that in my system and go the dual boot route. My computer asks me what drive I want to boot from when it powers on, couldn’t be easier. Based on the suggestions from /v/technology I decided to use Linux Mint (Cinnamon). The install was really straight forwarded. I loaded the .iso on a thumb drive and using a free tool made that thumb drive bootable. After the OS was up and running I needed to get the drivers for my recently upgraded Nvidia card (980Ti). I upgraded from an AMD R9280 a week ago solely based on Nvidia drivers having what I perceive as better Linux support. I had a bit of trouble getting the drivers installed, but a quick internet search yielded plenty of help to get them installed once I figured out how to disable Xwindow. I promptly downloaded and installed Steam and was happy to report 68 of my games will work with Linux! Next up was to get my VPN provider configured for use on my machine. Once again a quick search yielded a step by step youtube video on how to install and configure my VPN. I’m about all setup and now I plan on using my Win7 machine just for non-Linux supported games.

Gaming on Linux has improved tremendously from years ago. I've gone from dual booting over the last year to pretty much using linux exclusively. Skyrim, for example, works damn near flawlessly with Wine (even loaded with high def texture mods). A third of my steam library has native linux versions that "just work" out of the box. Most of the other games work fine with Wine. A very small selection of games are simply not playable - and usually a different game in the same genre runs fine. When you consider running emulators (since nearly all build versions for linux) there are thousands upon thousands of playable titles.

People like to say there are no big titles for linux natively but portal 2, minecraft, cs go, dota 2, civ 5, bioshock 3, xcom enemy unknown, all work out of the box with a single click install. Blizzard games work at near Windows performance with Wine (I've played ladder SC2, hardcore seasonal D3, raided HFC in WoD etc.

I'm excited for SteamOS - not because I will use it but just because it keeps promoting gaming on Linux in general. It has already gotten to the point where I can damn near fully switch over and I consider myself a fairly hardcore gamer.

For those games (and some programs) that aren't native linux, head on over to PlayOnLinux and take a look at the long list of what these great people have got up and running on linux systems.
